source.title: ScheduleFree+: Scaling Learning-Rate-Free & Schedule-Free Learning to Large Language Models

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Figure values are not numerically recoverable from the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies batch size and reports validation-loss outcomes for language-model training, bearing on V5, but uses Schedule-Free/AdamW comparisons rather than the claim’s original batch-size studies.
record.gate_note: Only the batch-size scaling experiments bear on a listed version. Other optimizer, weight-decay, warmup, averaging, and duration results concern Schedule-Free training against learning-rate schedules or other Schedule-Free variants; they do not measure the training–test gap or a listed version. Exact plotted losses are not stated in the text.
record.test_reason: The study's batch-size sweeps report held-out language-model loss and improvements from adapting momentum or averaging, bearing directly on V5 in a new optimizer setting. A training–test gap is not required by V5. The intended fixed-token comparison is described, but contradictory step counts prevent fully verifying the training budget.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the batch-size findings but is narrower than the paper's conclusion. The authors conclude that ScheduleFree+ combines momentum, adaptive Polyak steps and averaging changes into stable, anytime, learning-rate-free LLM training. They report consistent improvements over WSD and their strongest advantages over linear decay on long runs; shorter-run comparisons are mixed.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses LLM pretraining and validation loss, comparing Schedule-Free variants with AdamW and learning-rate schedules. It does not measure classification test error or training–test gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size and the presence of inner momentum change the reported validation-loss behavior; C-Refinement is less effective than inner momentum in the reported comparison.
record.problems: The batch-size results are presented in figures without numerical values in the supplied text. No uncertainty estimates are stated. The study measures validation loss, not the training–test gap, and does not report an image-classification batch-size experiment.
record.rows_left_out: No other rows were left out. Other experiments compare learning-rate schedules, weight decay, warmup, averaging parameters, or loss curves, and do not measure a listed version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization in the same architectures and recipes.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under limited or broader tuning.

Image classifiers, longer training as a remedy, normalization changes, and matching small-batch accuracy within the same epoch budget. Actual equality of token budgets across the batch sweeps cannot be verified from the contradictory configurations.
Dropout in classifiers, small-data regimes, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: No numerical losses or uncertainty estimates can be recovered for these sweeps. The text's qualitative findings suffice for conditional verdicts. Figures 2 and 3 should be interpreted as batch-size and recipe comparisons, not evidence about a training–test gap. The appendix lists constant tokens and constant steps while varying batch size, so it cannot substantiate both budget descriptions simultaneously.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence; no random-label or classification experiment.
Network width beyond interpolation and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD on held-out benchmarks.

Image classifiers; comparisons at a fixed epoch budget; longer training and normalization or regularization adaptations; accuracy matching within the same epoch budget. The text describes batch-scaling trends but provides no numerical values recoverable from its figures.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out classification error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: 120M parameter Llama 3 architecture transformer
rows.stage_stated: pretraining; warm-started from the same 2B token checkpoint
rows.operation_detail: Batch-size sweep comparing AdamW with a Linear-Decay schedule against Schedule-Free AdamW without inner momentum; both use square-root learning-rate scaling.
rows.note: The text says Schedule-Free falls behind at larger batch sizes and reaches a scaling cliff at 2M tokens per batch; AdamW has a similar cliff at 4M. Exact plotted loss values are not stated.
rows.check: The text explicitly reports scaling cliffs at 2M tokens per batch for Schedule-Free and 4M for AdamW; unavailable plotted values do not make this merely partial. Split the two optimizers into separate rows and record the qualitative results. The simultaneous conditions of 7.8B tokens, 15,000 steps and varying batch size are inconsistent; the actual step counts need clarification.

rows.subject: 120M parameter Llama 3 architecture transformer
rows.stage_stated: pretraining; warm-started from the same 2B token checkpoint
rows.operation_detail: Batch-size sweep comparing AdamW with a Linear-Decay schedule against Schedule-Free AdamW with inner momentum (β1 = 0.75); both use square-root learning-rate scaling.
rows.note: The text says inner momentum improves performance at small batch sizes and allows batch sizes of the same magnitude as regular AdamW; exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: The text explicitly reports improved batch-size robustness with inner momentum β1=0.75, reaching batch sizes comparable to AdamW. This supports V5's recipe-adaptation component, without establishing elimination of the large-batch penalty. Separate the adaptation comparison from the AdamW comparator. The fixed-token and fixed-step conditions are inconsistent.

rows.subject: 120M parameter Llama 3 architecture transformer
rows.stage_stated: pretraining; warm-started from the same 2B token checkpoint
rows.operation_detail: Batch-size sweep comparing Schedule-Free AdamW with C-Refinement against Schedule-Free AdamW with inner momentum.
rows.note: The text says C-Refinement enables training at larger batch sizes but is less effective than inner momentum; exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: C-Refinement enables larger batches but is less effective than inner momentum. The comparison does not establish complete removal of the penalty. Appendix C.5 reports inner momentum β1=0.9 for this figure, unlike Figure 2b's 0.75; record that distinction. Its reported 7.8B-token and 15,000-step budgets also conflict across varying batch sizes.

relationships.condition: 120M Llama-style model on FineWeb-EDU, reported approximately 8B-token batch sweep, square-root learning-rate scaling
relationships.reason: R1 reports large-batch scaling cliffs for both optimizers, consistent with workload-dependent batch limits; the fixed-token interpretation remains conditional on resolving contradictory step counts.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports sharp drops in performance as batch size increased, but this comparison remains unverified. Conflicting totals for training steps leave it uncertain whether the runs processed equal numbers of tokens.

relationships.condition: Schedule-Free training adapted with inner momentum or C-Refinement
relationships.reason: R2 reports that inner momentum permits larger batches comparable to AdamW; R3 reports a smaller improvement from C-Refinement, supporting V5's allowance for recipe-dependent mitigation.
relationships.display_finding: Inner momentum reportedly expanded the useful batch range, with a smaller improvement from C-Refinement, but these comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
